title: Bún bowl with chicken
skill: Setting out a bowl's parts in small dishes

notes.text: Soak the noodles in two pots, or in the pot in two batches.

move.title: A bowl built from small dishes
move.body: Bún is a Vietnamese bowl of cool rice noodles with chicken, crunchy vegetables, fresh herbs, and nước chấm, a sweet, sour, salty dipping sauce. Nothing here takes long to cook. The skill is setting every part out in its own dish first, then building the bowls.

why.title: Noodles that soak, not boil
why.body: Thin rice noodles only need hot water. Boiling them on the stove makes them mushy. Pour them into water that has just boiled, off the heat, and they soften in a few minutes.

why.title: Rinse them cold
why.body: Rice noodles turn sticky as they cool. A rinse under cold water washes off the starch and stops them cooking, so they stay separate.

why.title: Taste the sauce
why.body: Nước chấm balances four things: salty fish sauce, sour lime, sweet sugar, and water. Tasting and adjusting it is part of the recipe.

why.title: Every part in its own dish
why.body: When each part waits in its own dish, everyone can build a bowl the way they like it, and nothing gets soggy before it's eaten.

why.title: Wash after the chicken
why.body: Rotisserie chicken is already cooked, but it's still meat handled with your hands. Wash them before you touch the vegetables, and put the rest of the chicken in the fridge.

wrong.fix: Rinse them again under cold water, loosening them with your fingers.

wrong.sign: The noodles are still hard in the middle
wrong.fix: Leave them in the hot water 2 more minutes.
Add a spoonful of water and a squeeze of lime, then taste again.
Stir in a little more sugar, a pinch at a time.

choices: They soak in water that just boiled, off the heat

quiz.q: Why rinse the noodles in cold water?
What four tastes does nước chấm balance?
choices: Salty, sour, sweet, and water to soften them
quiz.explain: Fish sauce, lime, sugar, and water.

quiz.q: What do you do after pulling the chicken apart?

substitutions.note: Use 2 tablespoons of soy sauce. It's a different taste, but the sauce still works.

steps.text: Read the whole recipe. Set out a small bowl or plate for each part of the bowl.
steps.tip: Seven parts: noodles, chicken, lettuce, cucumber, carrots, herbs, and sauce.

steps.text: Set the saucepan on a back burner, handle in. Bring the noodle water to a boil.
steps.look: Big bubbles breaking all over the top.

steps.text: Turn off the burner. Add the noodles, push them under with the tongs, and let them soak.
While they soak, roll each lime on the counter, cut it in half with the paring knife, and squeeze the juice.
steps.tip: Rolling the lime first makes it juicier.

steps.text: Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, water, and garlic in the measuring cup until the sugar dissolves.
steps.look: No sugar grains on the bottom.

steps.text: Taste the sauce. Add more sugar, lime, or water, a little at a time, until you like it.
steps.tip: It should taste strong. It's a sauce, not a drink.

steps.text: Pour the noodles into the colander in the sink. Rinse them under cold water and shake them dry.
steps.look: Soft, white, cool noodles that pull apart.

steps.text: Pull the chicken meat off the bones with two forks and your fingers. Put it on a plate.
steps.look: Bite-size shreds, no skin or bones.

steps.text: Put the rest of the chicken in the fridge. Wash your hands with soap.
steps.tip: Clean hands before you touch the vegetables.

steps.text: Rinse the lettuce leaves, pat them dry, and tear them into bite-size pieces into a bowl.
steps.look: Pieces about the size of a cracker.

steps.text: Halve the cucumber the long way with the bridge grip, then slice it thin with the claw grip.
Set the knife down flat at the top of the board, blade facing away from you.
Rinse the mint and cilantro, pat them dry, and pull the leaves off the stems.
steps.tip: Tear big mint leaves in half.

steps.text: Put noodles in each big bowl. Add lettuce, cucumber, carrots, chicken, and herbs on top, side by side.
steps.look: Each part in its own section, like a wheel.

steps.text: Sprinkle peanuts on top if you're using them. Spoon sauce over each bowl just before eating.
steps.tip: Put the rest of the sauce on the table for more.
